correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from a unique decomposition of an idempotent \(F\) as a retraction onto \(U\) and a graph \(U\) over a subspace of \(\ker E\). Square-zero forces \(U\cap\operatorname{im}E=0\) and \(p(E(U))\subseteq U\cap\ker E\). Counting rank-\(b\) graphs and compatible retractions yields precisely \({n\brack r}_q q^{r(n-r)}{n-r\brack s}_q{r\brack b}_q\prod_{i=0}^{b-1}(q^s-q^i)q^{s(n-s)-b^2}\). All feasible ranges and zero-dimensional boundaries are included. Simultaneous conjugacy and standard Jordan classification yield uniform individual-target fibers. Independently reconstructed matrix multiplication checks cover 342 cells and 2378 target fibers. Finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The verified closest existence and prescribed-rank factorization literature does not give simultaneous finite-field counts of two *idempotent* factors with square-zero product or the exact factorization multiplicity for each given square-zero target. A related previously established idempotent-product rank census intersects here only at product zero and cannot determine nonzero square-zero fibers. The full two-factor rank and target-refined counts require the reversible transversality and retraction argument. Access limitations preserve explicit historical-priority risk; absence of a search match is not treated as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The three ranks of the factors and product are intrinsic, natural simultaneous factorization invariants. Distinguishing zero and nonzero square-zero products, the theorem supplies the complete count for every rank triple and each individual nilpotent target over every finite field. This is a substantive structural and enumerative classification, not a low-dimensional curiosity or routine restatement of rank-idempotent counts; the graph/transversality constraints explain exactly when square-zero products occur and how many factorizations each has.
